task.description:
Design the type coercion rules for the Expression DSL evaluator per DSL-05. Produce a design artefact at src/design/dsl-05-coercion.md covering:

1. Coercion table (6×6 matrix): for every pair of the 6 DSL types (null, bool, int64, float64, string, timestamp) and every operator category (arithmetic, comparison, boolean logic, unary negation), specify:
   - Whether coercion is automatic
   - The resulting type
   - Which operand (if any) is promoted
   - Any error condition

2. Key coercion rules (from requirement):
   - int64 ↔ float64 is automatic in arithmetic (int64 promoted to float64), never silent in comparison (comparison between different numeric types is an error, not silent coercion)
   - string to/from other types only via explicit built-in functions (never automatic)
   - null compared to anything except null returns null (three-valued logic)

3. Three-valued logic for null propagation:
   - null AND x → null
   - null OR x → null (if x is false/null) or true (if x is true)
   - NOT null → null
   - null in arithmetic operations → evaluation error
   - null in comparison (except null == null) → null

4. Evaluation strategy for each Node variant showing how coercion is applied at runtime

5. Updated evaluateNode() signature and dispatch table in src/expr/mod.zig

6. Coercion test matrix covering every type pair and every operator

Acceptance criteria: every type pair has a documented coercion behaviour; no silent coercion in comparisons; null semantics are fully defined.
acceptance_criteria: Coercion table covers all 6 types × all operator categories
No silent coercion in comparisons documented and enforced
Test matrix covering every type pair and operator is specified
Design maps directly to implementable evaluateNode() changes

result.summary: Design artefact for DSL-05 type coercion rules: 6×6 coercion matrix across arithmetic/comparison/boolean/unary operators, three-valued null logic, evaluation strategy per Node variant, updated evaluateNode() dispatch table, and comprehensive test matrix (90+ test cases).
result.next_action: Route to BACKEND-DEV (Step 2a) for implementation of evaluator with coercion logic
